prompt: The hero on this page looks flat and generic. Make it feel premium, like a specialty roaster's site.
The three product cards are just text. Give each one a visual so they actually sell the coffee.
Redesign this landing page with a warmer, more handcrafted feel. Go all out on the visuals.
Add an 'About the roastery' section with something visual that shows where the beans come from.
Northside Roasters needs a logo for the header. Make one.
Add a small icon to each product card: whole bean, ground, and cold brew. They should look like a set.
The page background is a flat colour. Give it a subtle recycled-paper texture behind the content.
Build a layered parallax hero where a mug, some beans and rising steam move at different speeds as you scroll.
Create a social share card for this page so links look good when posted on LinkedIn and X.
Add a friendly 404 page to the site with an illustration of a spilled coffee cup.
Generate a hero image of freshly roasted beans for this page and use it.
We want a little mascot character for the brand to use across the site. Create it and put it in the footer.
Fix the typo 'Roastres' in index.html.
The three product cards stack badly on tablets. Fix the grid so they sit two per row between 600 and 900px.
Check this page for accessibility problems and fix the contrast and the heading order.
Rewrite the hero headline and subheading so they are punchier. Keep each under 12 words.
Add a dark mode that follows the system setting, using CSS variables.
Add a newsletter signup form to the footer with email validation.
The page loads slowly. Add lazy loading and explicit width and height attributes to any images on it.
Add a small inline SVG bar chart comparing caffeine in the three coffees: 95, 120 and 200 mg.
